unit.title: Prepare for oxyacetylene/metal arc welding processes

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What should you do first when you are given a new welding job?
options: Read the drawing and job sheet carefully
Start cutting plate so as not to waste time
Set the machine to its highest current
Collect electrodes from any open packet

questions.stem: On a welding drawing, what does a triangle on the reference line of a weld symbol mean?
options: A butt weld
A spot weld
A fillet weld
A plug weld

questions.stem: On a weld symbol, what does a small circle where the arrow meets the reference line mean?
options: Drill a hole for a plug weld
Weld all the way round
Grind the weld flush
Make one tack only

questions.stem: On a weld symbol, what does a small flag where the arrow meets the reference line mean?
options: Grind the weld flat
Weld on the other side
Paint the weld afterwards
Weld it on site

questions.stem: Which is best for welding thin sheet steel of about 1 mm with simple workshop gear?
options: MMAW with a 5 mm electrode at high current
Oxy-fuel cutting with a large nozzle
Oxy-acetylene welding with a small nozzle
MMAW with a 4 mm electrode and a wide weave

questions.stem: Which process would you choose to weld 10 mm mild steel plate for a heavy gate frame at the Centre?
options: MMAW with suitable electrodes
Soft soldering with tin solder
Oxy-acetylene with the smallest nozzle
Silver brazing with a propane torch

questions.stem: How can you check that the plate supplied is the right thickness?
options: Judge it by eye from across the room
Weigh it on a bathroom scale
Tap it with a hammer and listen to the sound it makes
Measure it with a steel rule or vernier caliper

questions.stem: Why is a bevel (V preparation) cut on the edges of thicker plate before butt welding?
options: So the finished plate weighs less after welding
So the weld can reach right through the joint
So the joint needs no tack welds
So less PPE is needed during welding

questions.stem: Which tool is often used at the Centre to grind a bevel on a plate edge?
options: A hacksaw with a fine, sharp blade
A wire brush fitted in a power drill
An angle grinder and grinding disc
A centre punch and a ball pein hammer

questions.stem: Which of these should be removed from the joint area before welding?
options: Rust, paint, oil and scale
Only the paint; rust helps the arc
Nothing; the flux cleans it all
Only the oil; scale helps fusion

questions.stem: Why should chlorinated cleaning solvents (degreasers) never be used near arc welding?
options: They make the flux coating fall off the electrodes
They make the plate too slippery to hold
They turn the weld metal a green colour
Arc light turns the vapour into a poison gas

questions.stem: After cleaning plate with a degreaser, what should you do before welding?
options: Weld it straight away while it is wet
Let it dry fully and let the vapour clear
Wipe it over with an oily rag to protect it
Heat it with the torch to burn it off

questions.stem: Before hot work, why is the area checked for things that can burn?
options: Sparks can fly metres and start a fire
Anything that burns makes the arc wander and spit
They make the plate rust more quickly in storage
They block the light from the windows

questions.stem: What fire safety item must be ready near any welding or cutting job?
options: A full bucket of used engine oil
A box of clean cotton rags
A fire extinguisher of the right type
A large fan to blow the sparks well away

questions.stem: Why are screens placed around an arc welding bay?
options: To keep the welder warm on cool mornings
To stop the welding current leaking out
To hide the work from the assessor's view
To shield others from arc flash

questions.stem: Before fitting a regulator, what should you check on the cylinder valve outlet?
options: That it has been painted the same colour
That it is clean, undamaged and free of oil
That it feels warm to the touch from the sun
That it has a little grease on the thread

questions.stem: What is the right order of parts from an acetylene cylinder to the torch?
options: Cylinder valve, hose, regulator, torch, flashback arrestor
Regulator, cylinder valve, flashback arrestor, torch, hose
Cylinder valve, flashback arrestor, torch, hose, regulator
Cylinder valve, regulator, flashback arrestor, hose, torch

questions.stem: How should gas hoses be checked before use?
options: Look along their length for cracks and burns
Check only the end near the torch
Bend them hard to see if they snap
Smell them for leaks while the valves are shut

questions.stem: A bubble forms at the regulator joint during a leak test. What should you do?
options: Light the leak to burn the gas away safely
Carry on, as a small leak is quite normal
Shut the gas off and fix the joint
Wrap the joint tightly with insulating tape

questions.stem: Why are oxygen and fuel gas cylinders stored apart when they are not in use?
options: So their painted colours do not fade in the sun
So a fire at one is not fed by the other
So the store man can count them more easily
So they warm up in the sun at different rates

questions.stem: Before switching on an MMAW machine, which check is needed?
options: Cables are undamaged and the connections tight
The machine case has been painted quite recently
The electrode holder is warm from use
The work clamp is fixed to the machine case

questions.stem: Why must the work return lead connections be tight and clean?
options: So the cable looks neat and tidy on the bench
So the machine can be switched off more easily
So the electrode stays dry in the holder
Loose joints overheat and make the arc unsteady

questions.stem: Where do you find the right polarity and current range for an electrode?
options: On the label inside the welding helmet
On the label of the fire extinguisher
On the electrode packet or data sheet
On the steel maker's stamp on the plate

questions.stem: How should opened low-hydrogen electrodes (such as E7018) be stored?
options: In an open cardboard box on the workshop floor
In a warm electrode oven, as the maker says
In a bucket of water to keep them cool
Out in the sun on the window ledge to dry

questions.stem: Why is gas welding filler rod kept clean and dry?
options: Dry rods are lighter to hold and to carry
Clean rods give a brighter, hotter flame
Wet rods make the cylinder pressure rise
Rust and dirt on it can spoil the weld

questions.stem: Which tool is used to scratch a fine line on steel before cutting?
options: A pencil eraser
A paint brush
A scriber
A wire brush

questions.stem: Why should burrs and sharp edges be removed after cutting plate?
options: They cut hands and spoil the fit-up
They make the plate much heavier to lift
They make the arc too bright to look at
They change the colour of the finished weld

questions.stem: What is the root gap?
options: The width of the finished weld
The space between the plate edges at the root
The space between the welder and the work piece
The length of each tack weld

questions.stem: Why is the root gap kept even along the joint?
options: So the slag on top of the weld is easier to see
So the job needs fewer tack welds overall
So the plate cools down more slowly after
So penetration is even along the whole weld

questions.stem: Why is a butt joint sometimes set with a small angle (pre-set) before welding?
options: So the plates pull flat as the weld shrinks
So it looks better before welding
So the welding current can be lower
So rain runs off the finished job more easily

questions.stem: Which tool checks that two plates are at 90° to each other for a tee joint?
options: A long steel tape measure
A spirit level on its own
An engineer's square
A centre punch and hammer

questions.stem: How big should tack welds be?
options: As big as the finished weld, to save time
Small but well fused, to be welded over
Just a touch of the electrode, with no fusion
As long as possible, the full joint length

questions.stem: Which helps to control distortion when preparing a job for welding?
options: Clamps, balanced tacks and pre-setting
The largest electrode at the highest current
One long run from one end to the other
Leaving out the tack welds to save time

questions.stem: Why might a thick or high-carbon steel part be preheated before welding?
options: To make the old paint marks easier to see
To make the part lighter so it is easier to lift
To let you use a lighter helmet filter shade
To slow cooling and reduce cracking

questions.stem: How can you check the preheat temperature of a part?
options: By touching it lightly with a bare hand
By looking for a bright red glow
With a temperature crayon or thermometer
By dropping water on it to see it boil

questions.stem: Which PPE is needed when grinding a bevel?
options: Only a light paper dust mask
Glasses, face shield, gloves and ear muffs
A welding helmet with the dark filter down
A cap and a pair of dark sunglasses

questions.stem: Why should you check your gloves before welding?
options: Old gloves make the arc harder to strike
New gloves weigh less on the hands
Gloves must match the colour of the overalls
Holes or damp let in heat or current

questions.stem: What should be in place when welding or cutting indoors?
options: Good ventilation or fume extraction near the work
All doors and windows closed tight to keep heat in
A fan blowing fumes into the welder's face
A heater to keep the fumes warm

questions.stem: Why must galvanised (zinc-coated) steel be treated with extra care when welding?
options: The zinc makes the arc too quiet to hear clearly
Zinc fumes from the coating can make you ill
Galvanised steel cannot be cut or drilled
The zinc makes the plate strongly magnetic

questions.stem: What is a hot work permit?
options: A licence from the supplier to buy oxygen cylinders
A pass that lets you leave the workshop early
Written permission for hot work after safety checks
A note saying the plate is still hot

questions.stem: A machine has a tag on it saying 'DO NOT USE'. What does this mean?
options: It can be used by the instructor only
It is new and still in its box
It can be used if you are careful
It is faulty and must not be used

questions.stem: Why are the plate, consumables and job details written on the job card?
options: So the job can be traced and checked later
So the job looks more official
To use up spare paper in the store room
So the welder gets paid more for the job

questions.stem: How should a heavy steel plate be lifted?
options: Bend at the waist and jerk it up fast
Lift it high with one hand to save time
Knees bent, back straight, and get help
Drag it across the floor by a corner

questions.stem: Why should the work area be clean and tidy before welding?
options: So the instructor gives a better grade
To prevent trips, fires and lost tools
So the plate cools down faster
So the gas in the cylinders lasts longer

questions.stem: You find a crack in the gas regulator body while setting up. What should you do?
options: Use it with care, at a low pressure only
Tape over the crack and carry on
Swap it over onto the other cylinder instead
Stop, tag it out and tell the instructor

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan and prepare for a welding job from a drawing. What information do you need, and where do you get it?
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the drawing and the job sheet. From the drawing I find the sizes of the parts, the joint types and the weld symbols, which show the type and size of each weld and where it goes. From the job sheet or welding procedure I find the material and its thickness, the process to use (OAW or MMAW), the electrode or filler rod, and settings such as the current or nozzle size. I check the materials list and make sure the right plate and consumables are in the store, and I ask the instructor about anything that is not clear. Then I plan the order of work: marking out, cutting, edge preparation, cleaning, fit-up and tacking. I also plan for safety: PPE, the work area, fire precautions and ventilation, and I check that the equipment is in good order.
markingPoints: Reads the drawing for sizes, joint types and weld symbols
Gets the material, process, consumables and settings from the job sheet or procedure
Checks that materials and consumables are available, and asks about anything unclear
Plans the order of work from marking out to tacking
Plans the safety measures and equipment checks

essays.stem: Compare oxy-acetylene welding (OAW) and manual metal arc welding (MMAW). Say what each is best used for, and how you would choose between them for a job.
essays.modelAnswer: OAW uses a flame of oxygen and acetylene to melt the metal, with a separate filler rod. The heat is softer and easy to control, so it is good for thin sheet, small pipe and repairs, and the same set can be used for brazing, heating and bending. It is slow on thick plate and puts a lot of heat into the job, which can cause distortion. MMAW uses an electric arc between a flux-coated electrode and the work. The heat is concentrated and the process is quicker, so it is good for plate of about 3 mm and thicker, structural steel, gates and frames, and outdoor work. It is harder to use on very thin sheet because it can burn through. To choose, I look at the metal and its thickness, the position, the strength needed, the equipment and power available, and what the drawing or procedure says.
markingPoints: OAW: flame and separate rod; soft, controllable heat
OAW best for thin sheet, small pipe, repairs; slow and more distortion on thick plate
MMAW: arc and flux-coated electrode; concentrated heat, quicker
MMAW best for plate, structural work and outdoors; hard on very thin sheet
Chooses by thickness, position, strength, equipment and the procedure

essays.stem: Describe how to prepare two plates for a single-V butt weld: marking out, cutting, bevelling and cleaning.
essays.modelAnswer: Check the plate type and thickness against the drawing. Mark the sizes with a rule, square and scriber. Cut the plates to size with a guillotine, power saw or cutting torch, cutting on the waste side of the line, then remove the burrs. Mark the bevel line on the joint edge of each plate. Grind or flame cut each edge to the angle given, for example about 30° on each plate to give a 60° included angle, and leave a small root face of about 1.5–3 mm as the procedure gives. Check the angle with a bevel gauge or protractor, and check the root face is even along the edge. Clean the bevel and a band of plate on both sides of the joint to bright metal, removing rust, paint, oil and mill scale with a grinder or wire brush. Keep the cleaned plates dry until they are welded.
markingPoints: Checks the plate against the drawing and marks out accurately
Cuts on the waste side and removes burrs
Bevels each edge to the angle given and leaves an even root face
Checks the angle and root face
Cleans the bevel and both sides of the joint to bright metal

essays.stem: Describe how you make a work area safe before starting hot work (welding or cutting).
essays.modelAnswer: First check the area for anything that can burn, such as paper, rags, wood, oil or paint, and move it well away or cover it with a fire blanket. Check that sparks cannot fall through gaps in the floor or walls. Make sure a fire extinguisher of the right type is close at hand. Put up welding screens so that other people are protected from arc flash and sparks, and warn people nearby. Check the ventilation or switch on the fume extraction. Make sure the floor is dry and clear of trip hazards, that cables and hoses are laid safely, and that there is a clear way out. Check that gas cylinders are chained upright and away from the hot work. If the job is outside the normal workshop, get a hot work permit and arrange a fire watch.
markingPoints: Burnables removed or covered; gaps checked for sparks
Suitable fire extinguisher close at hand
Screens put up and people nearby warned
Ventilation or extraction checked; floor dry; cables, hoses and cylinders safe
Hot work permit and fire watch when working outside the workshop

essays.stem: Describe how to assemble and leak test an oxy-acetylene set, and the checks you make on each part.
essays.modelAnswer: Check that the cylinders hold the right gases, are upright and are chained on the trolley. Look at the cylinder valve outlets: they must be clean, undamaged and free of oil; wipe them with a clean, dry cloth if needed. Check each regulator for a cracked gauge, damaged threads or a missing seal, then fit it to the right cylinder: oxygen with a right-hand thread, fuel gas with a left-hand thread. Check that flashback arrestors are fitted to the regulator outlets. Check the hoses along their length for cracks, cuts and burns, and check that the clips are tight. Fit the torch with non-return valves and the right nozzle from the maker's chart. Release the regulator screws, stand to the side and open the cylinder valves slowly, then set the pressures. Brush soapy water on every joint, and fix any leak with the gas off before use.
markingPoints: Cylinders checked and secured upright; valve outlets clean and oil-free
Regulators checked and fitted to the right gas with the right thread
Flashback arrestors, hoses and clips checked and fitted
Torch with non-return valves and correct nozzle; valves opened slowly from the side
Every joint leak tested with soapy water and leaks fixed with the gas off

essays.stem: Describe how to set up an MMAW machine ready for welding, including the checks, connections, polarity and current.
essays.modelAnswer: Check that the machine stands on a dry, level floor with space around it for cooling air. Check the mains plug and cable for damage, and that the machine is connected to the supply as the maker requires. Check the welding leads for cuts or burnt insulation, and that the cable connectors are tight in the machine terminals. Check that the electrode holder's jaws and insulation are in good order and that the work clamp grips firmly with clean jaws. Connect the leads for the polarity the electrode packet asks for: on DC, electrode positive or electrode negative; on AC, polarity does not matter. Fix the work clamp to clean metal on the job or bench, close to the weld. Set the current within the range on the electrode packet for the size used. Switch on, strike a test arc on scrap plate and adjust the current if needed.
markingPoints: Machine on a dry, level floor with space for cooling
Mains cable, plug and welding leads checked; connections tight
Electrode holder and work clamp checked
Polarity set from the electrode packet; work clamp near the weld
Current set from the packet and tested on scrap

essays.stem: Explain how electrodes and gas welding filler rods should be chosen, stored and handled, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Electrodes and filler rods are chosen to match the parent metal, the strength needed and the process, as the drawing or procedure says: for example E6013 electrodes for general mild steel, or copper-coated steel rod for gas welding mild steel. The size is chosen to suit the thickness. Both must be kept clean and dry. Electrode flux takes in water from the air, and damp flux gives porosity, cracking and a poor arc, so electrodes are kept in their packets in a dry store, and opened low-hydrogen electrodes are kept in a heated oven as the maker says. Filler rods are kept in a dry rack or tube so that they do not rust or pick up oil. Handle them with clean, dry gloves, do not drop or bend electrodes because the flux can crack, and throw away any that are damp, rusty or damaged.
markingPoints: Chosen to match the metal, strength and process, as the drawing or procedure says
Size chosen to suit the thickness
Explains that damp or dirty consumables cause porosity, cracking or a poor arc
Stored dry: packets and dry store, oven for low-hydrogen electrodes, rack for rods
Handled with care, and damp, rusty or damaged ones thrown away

essays.stem: Explain how to fit up and tack a tee joint so that it is square and has the right gap.
essays.modelAnswer: Clean both plates where the weld will go. Mark a line on the base plate where the upright plate will stand. Stand the upright plate on the line and hold it with a clamp or a welding magnet. Check with an engineer's square, from both sides, that it is at 90° to the base plate. Check that the joint is tight along its length, or has the small, even gap the drawing gives, using a piece of wire of the right size as a guide. Put a small, well-fused tack at one end, check the square again, then tack the other end, and add tacks along a longer joint. Tack on the side away from the main weld if the procedure allows. Check again after tacking and correct the joint before welding if it has moved. Clean the tacks ready for welding.
markingPoints: Cleans the plates and marks the position line
Holds the upright with a clamp or magnet
Checks it is square with an engineer's square
Sets the joint tight or with an even gap as drawn
Tacks in a sensible order and checks again after tacking

essays.stem: Explain why distortion happens, how it can be controlled while the job is being prepared, and why preheat may be used.
essays.modelAnswer: Distortion happens because the weld and the metal near it expand when hot and then shrink as they cool, and the shrinking pulls the parts out of line. During preparation it can be controlled by cutting accurate parts and making good edge preparations, so that less weld metal is needed; by clamping parts to a bench or jig; by tacking in a balanced order, for example at each end and then the middle, or on opposite sides; and by pre-setting parts at a small angle so that the weld pulls them straight. Planning a balanced welding order also helps. Preheat means warming the parts before welding. It is used on thick sections, high-carbon steels and cast iron, because it slows the cooling and so reduces the risk of cracking and hardening near the weld. The temperature is checked with a temperature crayon or thermometer, as the procedure gives.
markingPoints: Explains expansion and shrinkage as the cause
Clamping and jigs
Balanced tacking order and accurate parts so less weld is needed
Pre-setting the parts
Preheat slows cooling to reduce cracking, and is checked with a crayon or thermometer

essays.stem: Explain what you should do if you find faulty equipment or the wrong materials while preparing for welding, and why reporting matters.
essays.modelAnswer: If I find faulty equipment, such as a cracked regulator, a damaged hose, a cut welding lead or a broken electrode holder, I stop and do not use it. I switch it off or shut off the gas, put a 'do not use' tag on it so that no one else uses it by mistake, and tell the instructor what I found. If the plate, electrodes or filler rods are not what the drawing or job sheet asks for, for example the wrong thickness or type, I do not use them; I set them aside and report it. I write the problem on the job card or in the fault book. Reporting matters because faulty equipment can cause shocks, fires or explosions, and wrong materials can give a weld that fails in use. It also means the fault gets fixed and there is a record of it.
markingPoints: Stops and does not use the faulty item
Switches off or shuts off the gas and tags the item out of use
Tells the instructor
Sets wrong materials aside and reports them; records the problem
Explains why: shock, fire or explosion risk, and welds that fail

practical1.title: Preparing and fitting up single-V butt joints and tee joints for MMAW
practical1.brief: As a group, set up a safe MMAW bay and prepare joints ready for welding from a simple drawing. Each member marks out and cuts two pieces of 10 mm mild steel plate, prepares the edges (a single-V bevel for a butt joint, or a square edge for a tee joint), cleans the joint area, then fits and tacks one joint while the assessor watches. Share the work so that the group makes at least two butt joints, with a root gap and pre-set, and two tee joints checked square. Every member also sets up the MMAW machine once: checks it, connects the leads for the polarity on the electrode packet and sets the current. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the joints are tacked and the area is clean.
materials: 10 mm mild steel plate, about 150 mm × 100 mm (2 pieces per member)
Job drawing showing the joints and weld symbols
Angle grinder with grinding and flap discs; bevel gauge or protractor
Steel rule, engineer's square, scriber, centre punch and soapstone
MMAW machine with leads, holder, clamp and 3.2 mm electrodes
G-clamps, wire for setting the root gap, and a wire brush
photos: The bay set up with screens, extinguisher and ventilation, and every member in PPE
Plates marked out from the drawing
A bevelled edge, showing the angle and the root face
A joint area cleaned to bright metal
A butt joint tacked, showing the root gap and pre-set
A tee joint tacked, with the square against it
The machine set up, with the leads connected and the current setting shown
All the joints laid out and labelled with each member's name
checklist: Wore full PPE, including a face shield and safety glasses when grinding
Read the drawing and marked out the parts to size
Ground the bevel to the right angle with an even root face (or squared the edge for a tee)
Cleaned the joint area to bright metal on both sides
Checked the machine and leads, connected the right polarity and set the current from the packet
Fitted and tacked the joint with an even gap, square or pre-set as needed
Left the area safe and tidy, with tools put away
safety: Check that the grinding disc is the right type, rated for the grinder's speed, and that the guard is on
Wear a face shield over safety glasses when grinding, and point sparks away from people
Tack only in a screened bay, and warn others before striking an arc
Clear burnables from the grinding and welding area; keep an extinguisher at hand
Switch off the machine before changing any connections

practical2.title: Assembling, leak testing and lighting an oxy-acetylene set, and preparing sheet for gas welding
practical2.brief: As a group, assemble an oxy-acetylene set from its parts: secure the cylinders on the trolley, check and fit the regulators, flashback arrestors, hoses, non-return valves and torch, and choose a nozzle from the maker's chart. Each member checks at least one part and tells the assessor what they checked and why. Then the group leak tests every joint with soapy water and sets the working pressures, and each member in turn purges the hoses, lights the torch, sets a neutral flame and puts it out. Finally each member cleans and prepares two pieces of 1.6 mm mild steel sheet for a butt joint (straight, deburred and clean) and tacks them, ready for welding. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the set is shut down and the area is clean.
materials: Oxygen and acetylene cylinders on a trolley with chains
Regulators, flashback arrestors, hoses with clips, non-return valves, torch and nozzle set
The right spanners, and leak-test solution or soapy water with a brush
1.6 mm mild steel sheet, about 150 mm × 50 mm (2 pieces per member)
Emery cloth, a file, firebricks and tongs
photos: Cylinders chained upright on the trolley, before the regulators are fitted
Hoses and torch connected, with the nozzle chart beside them
Soapy water on the joints during the leak test
Sheets prepared and tacked, ready for welding
The set shut down, with the hoses bled and coiled
checklist: Wore suitable PPE: tinted goggles, gloves, cotton overalls and boots
Checked a part for damage, oil and the right thread, and explained the check
Fitted parts to the right gas, with arrestors and non-return valves in place
Leak tested with soapy water and opened cylinder valves slowly, standing to the side
Purged, lit with a spark lighter (fuel gas first) and set a neutral flame
Prepared sheet edges straight, clean and deburred, and tacked them with an even gap
Shut the set down, bled the hoses and released the regulator screws
safety: Keep oil and grease away from all oxygen fittings; use clean, dry hands and tools
Keep the acetylene cylinder upright and both cylinders chained
Test for leaks with soapy water, never with a flame
Point the torch away from people and cylinders when lighting it
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for gas equipment
